method: Flesch Kincaid grade plus five, using a vowel-group syllable heuristic. Punctuated sentences and standalone task lines are counted as sentence units. Exact corpora and hashes retained. Quantity table fragments, headings, staff text, dates, lesson codes and the verbatim scheme outcome are excluded. Estimates guide editing; they are not learner assessments. Read-aloud and confirmed scribing routes are available.

Use the actual approved Week 4 design. The default pouch needs two matching pieces. Measure and recheck before cutting.
Find the ruler’s printed zero mark. Its physical end may come before zero. Keep the ruler still and flat. Read the line from directly above.
Mark 100 mm width and 120 mm height on each piece. Check each side again. These equal 10 cm and 12 cm. Ask the adult to approve the marks before cutting.
Measure 10 mm from the left, right and bottom edges. Mark the seam guide. Do not mark a closing seam across the top. Keep the pieces aligned for joining.
This card describes measurements. It is not a full-size cutting template. The pupil’s actual approved design controls any revised dimensions.

Wait for the adult’s approval before scissors, needles or adhesive are issued. Use the agreed support throughout the practical.
[ ] Adult checks actual design, tools, fabric and access needs before issuing equipment.
[ ] Use scissors and needles only with agreed adult supervision. Keep fingers clear of blade and needle exit points.
[ ] Count needles before and after. Keep them in a container. Never put needles or pins in your mouth or leave them in the pouch.
[ ] Pause with tools down and work safe. Stop for a missing or broken needle and keep the area clear. The adult recovers and accounts for every part and controls disposal. Do not release the pouch until all sharps are accounted for.
[ ] If bonding was chosen, use only adult-approved fabric adhesive after actual label checks. Follow its full cure time. No heat, irons or solvents are used in this lesson.
Recheck the marked line first. Keep the fabric flat and fingers outside the blade path. Use the locally approved scissor method. Turn the fabric to follow the line. Stop with scissors down before moving or asking for help. Pass and store scissors as the adult demonstrates.
Keep the needle in the work or its container. Keep fingers clear of the needle exit point. Count and return every needle at the agreed stop. Stop if a needle is missing or broken. Keep the area clear while the adult recovers and accounts for every part and controls disposal. Do not release the pouch until all sharps are accounted for. Never put pins or needles in your mouth.
Use prepared pieces or pupil-directed adult handling. If fabric or safe equipment is unavailable, rehearse using a paper model or empty hands and mark practical evidence pending.

Use this default method only when it matches the actual approved design. An adult demonstrates and supervises needle and scissor use. Use prepared pieces or adult handling if needed.
Put the two cut pieces together with edges aligned. Follow the 10 mm seam guide on the left, bottom and right. Keep the top open. Hold the layers together using only the adult’s approved method.
The adult selects a suitable needle and thread for the actual fabric. The adult shows passing thread through the needle eye and tying a small tail knot, or provides a prepared threaded needle. Start between layers and bring the needle out through the upper layer at the guide so the knot stays inside. Do not force an unsuitable needle through dense fabric.
Move about 5 mm along the line and put the needle through both layers. Keep fingers clear of where it will come out. Bring it back through both layers about 5 mm further along. Pull the thread gently away from faces until it lies flat. Keep the fabric flat rather than gathered.
Repeat small even passes about 5 mm apart. Pause to check that both layers are joined and the edges still align. Turn the work at a corner while the needle is safe. Join the left, bottom and right only. The top stays open.
The adult demonstrates on the back: take a small stitch through both layers, leaving a loop before pulling tight. Pass the needle through the loop and pull it snug. Repeat once. Trim the thread only using agreed scissors. Keep a short secure tail and avoid cutting the seam.
Count and return every needle. Check both layers are joined, the thread lies flat, the three edges hold together and the top is open. Do not rush to finish when time runs out. Store unfinished work safely for Week 6.
Use an adhesive route only if it is in the actual approved design and the adult has checked the fabric, product label, ventilation and access needs. Follow that label for application and full cure time. Do not invent a curing time or test an uncured join. No heat or solvents are used. Keep joining or testing pending where needed.
An adult can handle the needle while the pupil directs each action. Keep that role clear in the record. A prepared demonstration sample may support explanation but is not the pupil’s own completed join.
With no fabric or safe tools, use a paper model or empty-hand rehearsal. Mark imagined measurements, explain the cut line and trace the running stitch route. Record this as planning or simulation. Keep textile measuring, cutting and joining evidence pending until those actions happen on actual fabric with approved tools.

Use a real ruler on the actual work. In your book, copy the checks you use and add actual values and units. These ranges help you improve the product. They are not pupil grades.
Piece A width ___ mm and height ___ mm. Piece B width ___ mm and height ___ mm. Seam guide from edge ___ mm. Actual design target if revised ___. What I measured myself ___. Adult help ___.
I joined left / bottom / right ___. The top is open yes / not yet ___. Both layers are joined yes / not yet ___. Thread lies flat yes / not yet ___. Actual join method ___. Any cure still pending ___.
One real difference from the plan was ___. I rechecked it by ___. A safe correction or next step is ___. Do not trim or unpick until the adult checks that action.
Examples: 103 mm is outside the 98 to 102 mm width range. A 7 mm seam margin is outside the 8 to 12 mm range. A revised design uses its own recorded targets.

Weekly outcome verbatim: TEXTILES: measure, cut and join accurately.
I can use my checked design to measure, cut and join accurately with safe support.
[ ] I can mark and check two pieces before cutting.
[ ] I can use the agreed cutting and joining method safely.
[ ] I can check an actual measurement and record a useful change.
Make a small reusable pouch to hold three paper prompt cards, each 60 mm by 80 mm. Leave the top open. Join the sides and bottom. It should hold the cards upright, have no loose sharp parts and be comfortable to handle.
Default plan: two pieces, each 100 mm wide by 120 mm high. This is 10 cm by 12 cm. Mark a seam line 10 mm inside the left, right and bottom edges. Keep the top open. Use the pupil’s actual approved Week 4 design if it differs.
Check the design. Measure from zero. Mark and recheck. Cut with approval. Align and join. Return tools and record actual checks.
Use the check ranges to notice a difference and agree a correction. Keep actual measurements, support and any unfinished work visible. Do not claim a pupil cut or stitched where an adult did that action.
In your book. Rehearse in any language. Safe pauses use tools down and work protected.
